h1: Supalai Pasak Resort & Spa — a riverside bungalow resort on the Pa Sak that gives you quiet as a gift
intro: Drive a little out of Saraburi town towards Kaeng Khoi and the road quietens down, until you turn through the gate of Supalai Pasak Resort & Spa and find low bungalows scattered across a wide garden on the banks of the Pa Sak River. This is not a brand-new build but a long-running resort on a large plot, with mature shade trees kept well. It has an outdoor pool, a spa, an observatory and a riverside restaurant — bungalows start from approx. THB 1,600/night, often with breakfast.

A bungalow room interior with a large bed and a simple, comfortable country-resort feel
Buildings and gardens of the riverside resort on the Pa Sak, showing how green the grounds are

body.html: What guests mention most about Supalai Pasak is the space and the quiet. The resort sits on a large riverside plot, and the bungalows are not built in a tight row like a town hotel — they are spread across the garden, so each one feels private. Open your door and you see trees, not the next-door verandah. That is exactly why Bangkok families and weekenders drive out here to escape the noise.

Rooms come in several types, from the Pasak Standard up to suites and a villa. Many look out onto garden, river or mountain. Interiors are simple, with a TV, a mini-fridge and a bathroom with a tub. Rooms are larger than many expect at this price, and quiet because each is a separate bungalow. But honest guest reviews note that some units are older — curtains that do not close fully, fittings that have seen years of use. If you expect everything to feel brand new, this resort may not match that picture.
"Walked by the river in the cool early morning, so quiet you could hear the birds. The room wasn't fancy but it was spacious and clean, and the staff were lovely — far more helpful than we expected."

The thing praised in almost every review is the staff. On Booking, the Staff sub-score reaches 9.0, clearly above the resort's overall score. Many guests describe the team as warm and genuinely willing to help, from check-in to suggesting things to do nearby. For a country resort built around relaxation, that kind of sincere service is what brings people back for a second stay.

There is plenty to keep you busy for a resort this size — a large outdoor pool, a spa and massage rooms, a sauna, a tennis court, a billiards room, karaoke, and an observatory that is a genuinely distinctive touch. Kids can swim, adults can wander by the river or unwind with a massage. The riverside restaurant serves Thai food, and breakfast earns warm praise — making this a good fit for families or groups of friends who plan to spend most of the trip inside the resort.

On location, let us be clear: this place is out of town. It is around 20 minutes' drive from Saraburi town, and there are few restaurants or convenience stores within walking distance. On Booking, the location and value sub-scores sit around 6.7, which reflects that without your own car this would be awkward. But flip it around and that remoteness is precisely what buys the quiet — if you have come to relax in the resort rather than explore the town, the distance is a plus.

Distilling the real reviews: Supalai Pasak Resort & Spa suits travellers who want a wide, quiet riverside resort at an accessible price for a weekend break with the family. There are on-site activities, the staff look after you well, and breakfast is solid. The trade-off is a portion of rooms that show their age, and a location that needs a car. Understand that before you book — and pick a renovated room — and it is a worthwhile riverside stay on the Pa Sak.

A tip from reading across several review sources: ask for a renovated room with a river or garden view — message the resort directly when you book. Families should ask for a room near the pool. And if you come in the cool season (Nov–Jan), the riverside air is lovely and the atmosphere is at its best, so book ahead because it is a popular time.

faqTitle: FAQ — Supalai Pasak Resort & Spa, Saraburi

faq.q: Where is Supalai Pasak Resort in Saraburi, and how do you get there?
faq.a: The resort is at 79 Group 1, Adireksarn Road, Tha Khlo, Kaeng Khoi, on the Pa Sak River. It's about 15 minutes' drive from Kaeng Khoi town and around 20 minutes from Saraburi town. There are few shops nearby, so a car is recommended and it's wise to buy essentials before you arrive.

faq.q: How much does Supalai Pasak Resort cost, and what rooms are there?
faq.a: Prices start from approx. THB 1,600/night for a Pasak Standard, often including breakfast for two. There are several room types — Superior Suite, Deluxe Suite and Villa — rising to around THB 3,500. Prices vary by date and package, so compare a few platforms before booking.

faq.q: Who is Supalai Pasak Resort best for?
faq.a: It suits families and groups of friends who want a quiet riverside resort to relax in. There's a pool, spa, sauna, tennis court and an observatory all on-site. It's best for travellers with a car who want to escape the noise for a weekend, rather than tourists who want to explore the town on foot.

faq.q: What facilities does Supalai Pasak Resort have?
faq.a: It has an outdoor pool, a spa, massage rooms, a sauna, a tennis court, a billiards room, karaoke, an observatory and a riverside restaurant. The wide grounds along the Pa Sak are nice for walks, and breakfast is praised in many reviews.

faq.q: What are the rooms like — are they old?
faq.a: Rooms are separate garden bungalows — spacious and quiet — with a TV, fridge and a bathroom with a tub. Honest reviews note some units show their age, with curtains that don't close fully. It's worth messaging the resort to request a renovated room when you book.

faq.q: When is the best time to stay at Supalai Pasak Resort?
faq.a: The cool season (November–January) is best — the riverside air is pleasant and the atmosphere is at its finest, and on clear nights you can stargaze from the observatory. It's a popular family time, so book ahead, especially over long holidays.
